ConsumerContact: For additional information, consumers can contact DeWalt toll-free at (866) 854-5214 between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday, or visit the firm's Web site at www.dewalt.com
Description: This recall involves DeWalt DW378G and DW378GT 7 ¼-inch framing saws with date codes 200301-49 through 200637-49. The model numbers for the framing saws are located on the side of the housing. The date code is located either on the name plate or under the handle near the power cord exit. Circular saws involved in this recall have model number DC300 with date codes 200601-49 through 200637-49. The model number on the circular saw is located on the name plate on the top of the motor housing. The date code on the circular saw is located on the underside of the motor housing. Framing saws marked with a "V" on the underside of the handle near the cord set and circular saws marked with a "V" on the underside of the motor housing or under the handle where the battery is inserted have already been repaired and are not involved in this recall.

Hazards.Name: The lower blade guard can fail to close, leaving the blade exposed and presenting a laceration hazard to consumers.

Injuries.Name: DeWalt has received four reports of the lower guard failing to close, including three reports of lacerations. One consumer received lacerations to the hand and two others received lacerations to the leg, all required medical attention.

Manufacturers.Name: DeWalt Industrial Tool Co., of Towson, Md.

Products.Name: DeWalt DW378G/DW378GT Framing Saws and DC300 Circular Saws
Products.NumberOfUnits: About 97,000 framing saws and 37,000 circular saws

Remedies.Name: Consumers should stop using the saws immediately and contact DeWalt for a free repair.

Retailers.Name: Major home centers and hardware stores nationwide from January 2003 through August 2006 for about $170 for the framing saw. The circular saw was sold from May 2006 through September 2006 for between $380 and $800, depending on the kit.

Title: DeWalt Recalls Framing Saws and Circular Saws for Laceration Hazard
